Please describe in detail the steps you did to set up the account in Thunderbird. Did you use the Thunderbird Account Hub with automatic account setup, or manual configuration?

This week I have tried the same passkey as "Normal Password"

Please explain what that means. Passkeys and passwords are not the same thing, and are not interchangeable. https://www.passkeys.io/

I thought I might change the passkey, but now I cannot FIND how to change, remove or create a passkey.

You can create a passkey in your Yahoo Account Settings - Security. There is no point changing a passkey though. https://login.yahoo.com/account/personalinfo

For AT&T accounts you'll have to create a secure mail key. This is like an app password, but it isn't a passkey though. https://www.att.com/support/article/email-support/KM1240308/

Also, please post your Troubleshooting Information. At the top right of the Thunderbird window, click the menu button ≡, then select Help > Troubleshooting Information. Press the "Copy text to clipboard button" and paste the information into your reply.

content:
Using the settings downloaded by Thunderbird. https://autoconfig.thunderbird.net/v1.1/hotmail.com They are correct, and include oauth for SMTP. So if you are modifying them it is probably the issue, if you are using anything earlier that the current ESR branch of Thunderbird then connection failures for Microsoft sites is more than probable. The current release of Thunderbird does not use IMAP or SMTP when connecting to Hotmail/office365 it uses the Microsoft Graph framework

The next the most common cause of account setup failure lives in the antivirus products installed in addition to Windows defender.

  • The download of settings does not complete because the antivirus product blocks Thunderbird accessing the internet (firewall component)
  • The connection does not verify (because antivirus is trying to scan a connection that has no emails. Ooops)
  • The dialog to authenticate does not open in the web browser. Problems with passing links via the operating system Look at the anti phishing tools your antivirus installed.
  • You account approval from the browser does not update into Thunderbird. Multiple common issues here;
  1. The antivirus is blocking the Local-host adapter.
  2. There is another program on the system that is consuming data on that adapter (usually a development environment or web server product, Apache et. al.)
  3. You have cookies disabled in Thunderbird or the web browser. (Enable cookies)

Then you have the "other" issues caused by the tenants in business solutions (not all office365 is the same) choices as to what software can access their exchange and if they are going to support SMTP and IMAP/POP. Some business users are restricted to only use Microsoft Outlook for instance. This is an exceedingly complex area made that way by Microsoft.

Now the expectations of Microsoft as to how you may connect to their services has changed significantly since Thunderbird 115 was released. But there is a support article on that, have you read it? https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/microsoft-oauth-authentication-and-thunderbird-202

Fundamentally I would not expect Thunderbird 115 to connect to Hotmail using oauth at all successfully. There have been many Microsoft specific changes since the 2023 release of version 115.

content:
Repairing only re-indexes what Thunderbird has, or in the case of IMAP checks for the latest versions on the server and deletes everything pending the new downloads.

SO, I am guessing you are having connectivity issues that have extended far further than you anticipate. What exactly is this timeout issue? DO you have an antivirus scanning mail? Disable mail scanning as a first move to see if that is the cause of the timeouts. (it often is) and clean up the system temp folder (that can cause the system to slow to the point of timeouts. General instructions follow.

  1. Press Win + I to open Settings.
  2. Click on System, then select Storage on the left menu.
  3. Click on Temporary files under your main drive (usually C:).
  4. Wait for Windows to finish scanning your system.
  5. Check the boxes next to the temporary items you want to remove (such as Temporary files, Recycle Bin, or Windows Update Cleanup).
  6. Click Remove files.

content:
Thank you for your help! I have managed to resolve the issue.

--Original problem:--

I was unable to send emails from my personal Outlook.com account through Thunderbird, although receiving emails through IMAP and sending emails directly through Outlook.com on the web both worked normally.

I had previously been able to send emails through Thunderbird, but the last successful attempt was more than a year ago.

My SMTP settings were: - Server: smtp-mail.outlook.com - Port: 587 - Connection security: STARTTLS - Authentication method: OAuth2

Microsoft OAuth2 sign-in completed successfully, but sending still failed. Thunderbird's Error Console showed:

- `535 Authentication unsuccessful` - `Error during AUTH XOAUTH2, sending empty response` - `500 Unrecognized command 'Length: 7'`

    • Troubleshooting performed:**

1. Verified the SMTP settings and changed the authentication method to OAuth2. 2. Restarted Thunderbird and refreshed the saved authentication credentials. The error persisted. 3. Contacted Microsoft Support, but they referred me back to Thunderbird without identifying the cause. 4. Temporarily disabled Trend Micro Maximum Security to test whether antivirus interference was responsible. The exact same errors persisted. 5. Confirmed that my VPN was disconnected during testing, making VPN interference unlikely.

    • Solution:**

I eventually discovered that my Microsoft account's primary alias was different from the Outlook.com email address I had configured as the SMTP username in Thunderbird. My primary alias is a different email address that I used when I registered for my Outlook email.

I changed the **SMTP username in Thunderbird to my Microsoft account's primary alias**, without changing the SMTP server, port, security, or OAuth2 authentication method.

After making this change, Thunderbird successfully sent emails!

Importantly, I did not need to change my Microsoft account's primary alias or reconfigure my incoming IMAP settings.

This appears to be the same solution described by another user in [Mozilla Bug #1917321](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1917321).

For anyone experiencing the same problem, I recommend checking whether the SMTP username matches the Microsoft account's primary alias, especially if the account has multiple email aliases.

Thank you again for your assistance. I hope this information helps others encountering the same SMTP authentication error.
